adaptations.withheld: sacred or restricted dance: no teaching adaptations

social_formats.description: A trio performance involving a horse dancer, a male lead, and a male in female attire.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Often used to steady the horse frame or gesture during the narrative song.
movement_profile.footwork: Rhythmic stepping to mimic horse movements; specific counts not described in sources.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Open village spaces; the horse moves through the crowd or in a central performance area.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Torso is encased in the horse frame; movement is generated from the legs and hips to tilt the frame.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Ground-level rhythmic stepping; no high jumps described.
movement_profile.partnering: Trio interaction between the horse dancer, the Rauta, and the Rautani.
movement_profile.posture: Upright, with the weight of the bamboo horse frame supported by the shoulders.

signature_moves.description: The dancer inside the frame mimics the galloping and prancing of a horse.
signature_moves.name: Ghoda Nacha

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid mishandling the horse frame, which is a consecrated ritual object.

music_profile.sound_description: The sound is characterized by the high-pitched, piercing melody of the mahuri wind instrument over the deep, resonant rhythmic patterns of the dhola drum, accompanied by vocal storytelling.
music_profile.vocal_style: Folk songs performed by male leads (Rauta and Rautani)

basic_steps: Anointing the bamboo frame with vermillion and butter lamps
Stepping into the central cavity of the horse frame
Coordinating shoulder-strapped frame movement with rhythmic walking
Call-and-response interaction between Rauta and Rautani
Mimetic horse movements including galloping and turning
teaching.formation: Processional or central circle with the horse at the center
teaching.level_notes: Requires significant physical stamina to carry the bamboo frame for extended periods.
teaching.rhythm: Rhythmic patterns dictated by the dhola drum
